title: Claims Accounting Note on Voided Payments under the Larkspur Personal Umbrella Policy
content:
On a Larkspur Personal Umbrella Policy claim, a payment that has already been voided is never voided again.

An uncashed umbrella payment may be voided. Umbrella claim money issued on a claim is carried as the indemnity paid on that claim: each payment issued raises it, and each voided payment lowers it by the amount voided.

## How the rule is judged

Whether a payment has already been voided is read from the umbrella claim file, as it stands before any new void: a void entry names the payment it voids. A payment that some void entry already names has been voided, and no second void is made against it.

| The claim file shows, for the payment | Can the payment be voided? |
|---|---|
| No void naming it | The rule does not stand in the way |
| A void already naming it | No; it is never voided again |

## Hypothetical illustrations

- A hypothetical umbrella payment of $25,000 is issued and later voided while uncashed. The indemnity paid on the claim rises by $25,000 when the payment issues and falls by $25,000 when it is voided. That payment cannot be voided a second time.
- A hypothetical claim carries two payments, one of which has been voided. The rule bars only a second void of the voided payment; it says nothing about the other payment.
